recipes.name: Apple Crisp
ingredients_raw: 10 cups all-purpose apples, peeled, cored and sliced

steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Place sliced apples in a 9x13-inch baking dish. Mix white sugar, 1 tablespoon flour, and cinnamon together; sprinkle over apples. Pour water evenly over apples.
Combine oats, 1 cup flour, brown sugar, baking powder, and baking soda in a large bowl. Add melted butter and mix with a fork until crumbly; sprinkle evenly over apple mixture.
Bake in the preheated oven until apple filling is bubbling, and top is golden brown, crisp, and caramelized around the edges, about 45 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Apple Crisp
raw_recipe.description: This apple crisp recipe bakes a layer of sliced apples with a deliciously crunchy brown sugar and oat topping for a comforting fall dessert.

video.description: Try this baked recipe that uses common pantry items to make a decadent crumbled dish! In this video, Nicole shows you how to make one of the all-time best fall desserts, apple crisp. Using peeled, cored, and sliced apples, coat the apple slices in both a cinnamon-sugar mixture and a buttery oat topping. This autumn delight bakes in the oven until golden brown and bubbly. In under an hour, this easy-to-make and tasty Thanksgiving treat is ready!

review.reviewBody:
Oh my gosh, this is delicious! I have never had such a delicious apple crisp! I will never search for another recipe! I fixed this for my large, picky family for Thanksgiving. There were no leftovers!:-) Here's what I changed. I made 2 batches. In one, I added 1/4 cup of water rather than 1/2 cup. That was perfect. In the other batch I didn't add any water at all, and it was a little drier than I like. So cut the water in half. Also, I tossed the apples in the cinnamon and sugar mixture, and I added some nutmeg to that mixture. I think that's what made the apples soooo perfect. Lastly, I doubled the crust recipe and put a layer on top and on bottom. Yum!!! I used 6 large Granny Smith's. I won't change a THING about this recipe next time I fix it, which if my family has anything to say about it, will be tomorrow!:-) 
11-13-06 I made this again for like the 5th time. It's still good, but I think next time I will try to cut the butter into the crust rather than melt it. My crust is never "crumbly" like I like on a crisp recipe. Still a 5-star no doubt!!!

Excellent recipie. It is important to follow the steps and not deviate from them (i.e. don't mix up All the ingredients at once and throw it over the apples as you may be able to get away with in other crisp recipes)
The recipie was great. the water factor wasn't a factor for me. it turned out to be a very nice thick juice that accented the dish nicely.
A word of caution when using this or any apple crisp recipie. THE TYPE OF APPLES DO MATTER. I made this twice. Once with Red Delicious apples. these apples are not the greatest to use as they are often soft and bland. the recipe was great but the apples lacked. I then used Granny Smith green sour apples. This made All the difference! Do not be afraid to use sour apples. Keep in mind you are using two cups of sugar in this recipie and it will be quite sweet. It simply comes down to the need for a hard and sour or at the very least sharp tasting apple to counter the sugar and even the flavor out. It will taste much better. Do not use soft or bland tasting apples, and do not overcook as the apples will turn mushy if you overcook. If you fear overcooking then cut your apple thicker. If you like the very thin slices of apple then you need to you a very hard, fresh, tart apple. I do not suggest using Red Delicious apples. I also addeed a pinch of nutmeg.

I submitted this recipe several years ago, before I was a registerd member. It was included in the first cookbook that All Recipes published, and I was so proud. I like to come back every now and then to read some reviews. I recommend Granny Smith apples; it won't be too sweet or watery. Thanks to all you cooks for your ratings and reviews!

Tasted wonderful. I followed the directions exactly this time, but in the future I will make the following changes: cut the amount of water in half, double the topping and add 1/4 teaspoon of nutmeg. You may need to increase the cooking time as mine was not done in 45 minutes. Great recipe though!

This recipe is nearly the exact recipe I've been using for years, so I had to add my review to the pile. It is my favorite way to get rid of an apple surplus (I ususally use about 7 good sized apples of mixed variety, minus what I snack on while I make it). The only things I do differently are:
 
1) I use 1/2 brown sugar and 1/2 white for the apple mixture. 
2)I add fresh ground nutmeg, vanilla extract, and often raisins. 
3)I omit the h20 and 
4)I always add a heaping spoonful of gourmet butterscotch caramel ice cream topping to the apple mix-TRUST ME on this one! 

In the begining, I had a hard time with my crumble mix being 'crumbly' until I figured out to lightly press it down into the bowl, chill it for at least 30m and then break it up with a fork. Letting the butter in the mix re-harden really makes a BIG difference in the final crumble factor. Also, you must use real butter, margarine won't have the same effect for this recipe. I'll often assemble this earlier in the day and leave it in the frige, then just before dinner, break up the crumble, top and bake while we eat. I always serve with vanilla bean ice cream and have ALWAYS gotten rave reviews with this one.

I'm adding my notes and changes here in a review, since I lost them when they discontinued the dinner spinner app. Hopefully someone else can benefit from them too! I typically use half granny smith and half honey crisp apples. Little to no water over top in step 3, just a small sprinkling at most. Sometimes I add a little bit of nutmeg in with the cinnamon, depending on my mood. And then I double the amount of crumble topping. And since I double the crumble, I usually use a deep 9x13 pan... Yummy!!

This is a delicious dessert! I read several reviews and made the following adjustments. My family absolutely loves it! 1. I soaked the Granny Smith apples in lemon juice and water as I peeled and prepped. 2. I added 1 tsp of nutmeg to the sugar, flour, and cinnamon apple topping. 2. I skipped the additional water and used 2 tsps of vanilla instead on top of the apples. 3. I added a cup of rolled oats to the quick oats for texture and additional coverage on top of the apples. 4. I used Kerry Gold butter. YUM!
I used granny smith apples and instead of water, used lemon juice (only 1 1/2 tsp). I also tossed the apples with the sugar (halved the amount), cinnamon, flour and lemon juice. Turned out great!

Delish, but I would make a few changes; next time I would only use 1/2 c of white sugar. I added lemon to keep apples from turning and added juice to recipe. Instead of adding crumb coat to top of apples, I will place on cookie sheet at 250 degrees, bake until crispy. Let cool and store in airtight container and sprinkle on top of each serving.

I gave this 5 stars because I changed a few things. If not, I would give it 2 stars. I reduced the white sugar by a lot. I used 2 tablespoons. I omitted the water all together. I doubled the toppings for the crisp. I added some vanilla and a little nutmeg in the apple mix before putting it in the pan.

The recipe needs 50% more butter. If you follow the recipe, the topping remains dry. 50% more butter is perfection. I also double the cinnamon. In my oven, I have to cook longer. So dont be afraid to check every 5 mins after the initial 45. It also stays crunchy even after refridgerating! So yummy!

This was a great recipe. The only thing I changed was to cook the thinly sliced apples till tender before using them. I used 1c butter, 1/2c brown sugar, 1/2c white sugar, punch of salt and cinnamon. Simmer until tender, then drain all the liquid. That way you dont have to add any water.

I love this recipe! When I make it I use half (at least) the white sugar and I double the topping mixture! My family loves it! And depends on how you like your oats.. more of a “crisp” I use the large flake oats or more mushier I use quick oats.. or you can do half and half!

Was looking for a recipe to use my home canned apple pie filling in. This worked great! Added 3/4 cup of chopped pecans to topping and only had to cook 30 minute, until it browned. Definitely a keeper.

3tbs of water was not enough to soften the apples fully. Using granny smith and honey crisp apples. It came out delicious just wasnt quite softened fully. I think they should go back to the half cup that they changed from. Making it again right now

Great recipie that anyone can make and everyone will love. I did make a few adjustments myself. I didn't use water at all, unnecessary in my mind; I think it makes it too runny and takes away from the flavors and dulls it down. I do however use a couple tablespoons on lemon juice instead of water as well as a tbsp of vanilla extract. As many others do, I also double the amount of crumble mix/toppping and also take a 2oz bag of walnuts and crush them with a rolling pin and sprinkle them on the crumble before I put it in the oven. It gives it a little extra something I can't explain but, it brings something special to it. Best served warm, in my opinion and should be topped with a little scoop on homemade vanilla ice cream, whipped cream or caramel sauce. Homemade is so easy to make and tastes so much better. I have run out of rolled oats one occasion and had to substitute using half rolled oats and half instant oatmeal and it didn't really make much difference. Also if you want/ or need to use less sugar, you can and add a little honey or REAL maple syrup. I have also substituted the white and brown sugar with Swerve white and brown sugars and it tastes just as good. My mother in law absolutely loves apple crisp and is a type 2 diabetic so when I know she's going to be partaking I use the swerve.
I use 1/2 cup of flour instead of the full cup. Excellent recipe!
My family and I loved 💜 this apple 🍎 crisp recipe 😊
Used gluten-free flour and Maple & Brown Sugar Instant Oatmeal.
Good
